newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile prepares law to end whiskey tax spat.
newsitem.headline: Chile prepares law to end whiskey tax spat.

text.p: Chile will publish within the next six weeks details of a new law to cut taxes on whiskey and end a long-running trade dispute with the European Union, said Deputy Foreign Ministry Mariano Fernandez.
"We are going to end the tax discrimination against whiskey," Fernandez told a news conference.
"This will be in line with World Trade Organization (WTO) rules."
Chile has imposed a 70 percent tax on whiskey since 1979, which has been the subject of constant complaints from whiskey producers.
The new law comes six months after Chile and the EU signed a new economic co-operation agreement which is expected to lead eventually to a free trade accord.
The EU filed a complaint to the WTO against Chile in 1995 charging that the tax on whiskey sales, including the Scotch variety, was a non-tariff trade barrier.
The most vocal supporter of the tax has been the Chilean association of pisco producers. Pisco, a popular local brandy, is taxed at 25 percent.
Fernandez declined to give details of the new law but said taxes on other alcoholic drinks would have to rise so that the new law would not reduce tax revenues.
"There will be modification of taxes on all other (drinks). The changes will be tax-neutral," he said.
